NFL DFS Quarterback Rankings: Week 12 (DraftKings)

DraftKings main slate · Sunday, November 29 · 9 games · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of November 24, 4:40 PM ET

Joe Burrow is the top-projected quarterback on the Week 12 DraftKings main slate at 24.4 DraftKings points for $7,700, against New Orleans. Jayden Daniels (20.9, $6,000) and C.J. Stroud (20.4, $6,500) are next.

Jayden Daniels returns the most per dollar among quarterbacks projected for at least 15 points: 3.48 projected points per $1,000 at $6,000.

Every projection is a SPAGS model estimate from the November 24, 4:40 PM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. This page updates each time the main-slate numbers are published.

Quarterbacks to know in Week 12

Joe Burrow, CIN vs NO ($7,700)

Joe Burrow carries the highest SPAGS model projection at the position, 24.4 DraftKings points at $7,700, the highest on the entire main slate. That is 3.6 points clear of Jayden Daniels. The salary works out to 3.17 projected points per $1,000, 2nd of 13 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Burrow averaged 24.4 points with a simulated floor of 9.3 and a ceiling of 44.4, and he holds 30% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Cincinnati is a 10-point favorite at home against New Orleans, with an implied team total of 30.25 in a game totaled at 50.5.

Jayden Daniels, WAS at ARI ($6,000)

Jayden Daniels projects 2nd at the position with 20.9 DraftKings points at $6,000, 4th on the main slate overall. The model includes 6.2 rushing attempts. The salary works out to 3.48 projected points per $1,000, 1st of 13 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Daniels averaged 20.9 points with a simulated floor of 8.2 and a ceiling of 38.4, and he holds 14% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Washington is a 7.5-point favorite on the road against Arizona, with an implied team total of 25 in a game totaled at 42.5.

Value: Justin Herbert, LAC vs NE ($5,300)

Justin Herbert projects for 16.4 DraftKings points at $5,300, which works out to 3.09 points per $1,000 of salary. That is the best rate of any player priced in the cheaper half of the 13 quarterbacks the model projects for 15 or more points. The model includes 4.5 rushing attempts. Across 10,000 simulations Herbert averaged 16.4 points with a simulated floor of 6.4 and a ceiling of 29.9, and he holds 2% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. The Chargers are a 1.5-point favorite at home against New England, with an implied team total of 18.5 in a game totaled at 35.5.
